content.key_idea: A central controller manages a set of VQA clusters that jointly optimize similar Hamiltonians and adaptively split into child clusters when their optimization trajectories diverge, before a post-processing step selects the best solution per Hamiltonian.

summary: TreeVQA is a tree-based execution framework for Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) that cuts shot counts by executing similar tasks jointly and branching only as their quantum executions diverge. This figure shows TreeVQA's architecture: a central controller receives task Hamiltonians, initial states, a shot budget and other settings, and manages a set of VQA clusters (drawn as stacked cards C_i, C_k, C_j), each jointly optimizing a mixed Hamiltonian over the tasks sharing an initial state; after iterations a Post-Processing step evaluates each Hamiltonian across all cluster states to output the optimal energy and quantum state per task. A callout below zooms into one VQA Cluster's inner loop, min(<H_mixed>), which feeds a Splitting? decision: if trajectories have not diverged it loops back to continue joint optimization, otherwise the cluster splits into two child clusters that inherit the parent's parameters.
